subject: Science
textbooks: Assessment of Practical Skills in Science, Class X (CBSE)
notes: Periodic Classification of Elements, Evolution, and Motor / Electromagnetic Induction / Electric Generator are taught but assessed only formatively; they are not in the year-end examination.

The document's note for teachers also lists 'Heredity and Evolution' as not assessed in the year-end examination, while Unit II's summative content still lists Heredity. Confirm with the school's exam coordinator before excluding Heredity.
Information in the NCERT textbook boxes is not assessed in the year-end examination.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
topics: Types of reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, precipitation
outcomes: Writes and balances chemical equations
Classifies reactions by type

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics: Acids and bases in terms of furnishing H⁺ and OH⁻ ions
pH scale and the importance of pH in everyday life
Preparation and uses of sodium hydroxide, bleaching powder, baking soda, washing soda and Plaster of Paris
outcomes: Identifies acids and bases using indicators
Relates pH to everyday phenomena
notes: Definition of pH relating to logarithm not required

chapters.name: Metals and Non-metals
topics: Formation and properties of ionic compounds
outcomes: Arranges metals by reactivity
Explains formation of ionic compounds and corrosion prevention

chapters.name: Carbon and its Compounds
topics: Covalent bonds: formation and properties of covalent compounds
Hydrocarbons: saturated and unsaturated; homologous series
Nomenclature of alkanes, alkenes, alkynes and compounds with functional groups (halogens, alcohol, ketones, aldehydes)
Chemical properties: combustion, oxidation, addition and substitution reactions
Ethanol and ethanoic acid (properties and uses only)
outcomes: Names carbon compounds by functional group
Describes the chemical properties of carbon compounds

chapters.name: Periodic Classification of Elements
outcomes: Traces the development of the periodic table

chapters.name: Life Processes
topics: Basic concept of nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion in plants and animals
outcomes: Explains nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion in plants and animals

chapters.name: Control and Coordination
outcomes: Distinguishes voluntary, involuntary and reflex actions
Explains hormonal coordination in plants and animals

chapters.name: How do Organisms Reproduce?
topics: Reproduction in animals and plants (asexual and sexual)
Reproductive health: need and methods of family planning
outcomes: Compares asexual and sexual reproduction
Explains the need for reproductive health

chapters.name: Heredity
topics: Mendel's contribution: laws for inheritance of traits
outcomes: Applies Mendel's laws to simple crosses
Explains sex determination
notes: See subject note: the teacher note lists Heredity as not assessed in the year-end examination

chapters.name: Evolution
outcomes: Distinguishes acquired and inherited traits

chapters.name: Light - Reflection and Refraction
topics: Reflection of light by curved surfaces; images formed by spherical mirrors
Centre of curvature, principal axis, principal focus, focal length
Refraction; laws of refraction; refractive index
Refraction by spherical lenses; images formed by lenses
Lens formula; magnification; power of a lens
outcomes: Uses the mirror and lens formulae
Applies the laws of refraction
notes: Derivations of the mirror formula and lens formula not required

chapters.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topics: Functioning of a lens in the human eye
Defects of vision and their corrections
Applications of spherical mirrors and lenses
Refraction of light through a prism
Scattering of light and applications in daily life
outcomes: Explains defects of vision and their correction
Explains dispersion and scattering of light
notes: Excludes the colour of the sun at sunrise and sunset

chapters.name: Electricity
topics: Resistance, resistivity and factors affecting resistance
Series and parallel combination of resistors and daily-life applications
Heating effect of electric current and its applications
Electric power; interrelation between P, V, I and R
outcomes: Applies Ohm's law
Computes equivalent resistance of series and parallel combinations
Relates P, V, I and R

chapters.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
topics: Field due to a current-carrying conductor, coil or solenoid
Force on a current-carrying conductor; Fleming's Left Hand Rule
outcomes: Applies Fleming's Left Hand Rule
Explains domestic electric circuits

chapters.name: Motor, Electromagnetic Induction and Electric Generator
outcomes: Explains the working of a motor and a generator

chapters.name: Our Environment
outcomes: Explains ecosystems and environmental problems
Distinguishes biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances
